preconditions.description: The integer n is between 2 and 300,000 inclusive.
The string s has length exactly n.

preconditions.expression: all('a' <= c <= 'z' for c in s)
preconditions.description: The string s consists only of lowercase Latin letters.

postconditions.description: The output indicates 'YES' if and only if there exists at least one pair of indices (l, r) with 1 <= l < r <= n such that reversing the substring s[l-1:r] results in a string lexicographically smaller than s.

postconditions.expression: not possible or (output_lines[0] == 'YES' and len(output_lines) == 2 and l_out >= 1 and r_out <= n and l_out < r_out and s[:l_out-1] + s[l_out-1:r_out][::-1] + s[r_out:] < s)
postconditions.description: If possible is true, the output starts with 'YES' followed by two integers l and r (1-indexed, l < r) such that reversing the substring from l to r yields a string strictly lexicographically smaller than the original string s.
If no such substring exists, the output is exactly 'NO'.
